In message <1191397976....@50g2000hsm.googlegroups.com>, IC-


The distinction being drawn is between:

- adapting your game in a way that will give you defences against a wide
variety of decks, which will also work against the Imbued

- adapting your deck in a way that will give you defences against the
Imbued.

For example, consider the Laibon.

Have you had to evolve your decks to deal with the new options that
Laibon players have? Sure, I can see players being perturbed by - say -
the Eldest Command Undeath, or by Tsunda/The Eldest are Kholo decks, or
all sorts of other decks. Have you tweaked your decks as a result -
perhaps using the new tech in Legacies of Blood? Sure, that seems
reasonable.

But, have you (the general you) been forced to put specific anti-Laibon
tech in a deck? Cards that won't work (or will be very, very weak)
against Camarilla decks, or against the Imbued, or the Sabbat, or a
mixed-clan deck, or...?

That's the problem that a number of people are seeing.

The problem is that a number of deck types can continue to use existing
tech against the Imbued, so some players won't see all that much of a
problem. Other decks don't have existing tech to use against the
Imbued, and the players of those decks object to being told to put in
specific anti-Imbued tech that won't see any use nine games out of ten,
but they'll be absolutely dead in the tenth game without it. If I never
see an ally deck, why should I put ten anti-Imbued cards in an S&B deck?
I don't need to against the Laibon - I use stealth, intercept, bounce
and everything else that I can use against everyone else. So if I don't
need specific anti-Laibon tech, why do I need specific anti-Imbued tech?
I don't need specific anti-Corruption tech to save me from Setites -
rush combat, intercept etc. will save me. I don't need specific anti-
Assamite/Contract tech, because I can use combat defence as usual.

If the answer for a given deck is "Put in some anti-Imbued cards", why
is it the case that I don't have to put in other specific anti-tech to
defend against other clans and sects?

I certainly do think that cards with incidental anti-Imbued effects are
good e.g. a combat card that is good, but particularly effectively
effective against Imbued/allies generally, or a vote that can hurt
anyone but will hurt Imbued/allies just a little bit more. And I do
think that if a particular deck finds it easier to cope with the Imbued
by including specific anti-tech (to cope with a particular metagame
shift, say) then it should have the options to (if it wants).

But that's all different from (some) deck-styles having to specifically
deal with the Imbued with anti-Imbued cards. And that's what a number
of players are objecting to being told to do.

Now, it's entirely possible that some of those players could adapt their
decks in a generic way that will help against Imbued - but they just
haven't worked out how (yet). But being told "Pack anti-Imbued tech"
feels like being told "Pack anti-Return to Innocence tech." If I need
to pack specific anti-tech, it's a good indication that something is
awry and should be discussed and investigated. It may turn out that you
can find the generic way, as part of that investigation. It may turn
out that the deck(s) having problems are substandard in a lot of other
ways too. But it may also turn out that there's a problem.

--
James Coupe

> Rush combat and intercept will "save" you against the imbued as well.

That's what everyone thought. Then they realised that it's not true.
Rush cards can be cancelled with Determine. Or Memories can be put on
the most dangerous rushing or blocking vampires each turn. They can be
recycled with Parthenon / Anthelios. Even assuming your rushes aren't
cancelled and your fighty vampires aren't Memoried, taking down an

unblockably (since it's not even an action). Also they are cheap, can
bloat easily, and multiply. Your scary combat dude might cost 6 or 7
(or more). Their dudes cost 3 or 4 or 5 pool, and they generally
quickly get out Travis / Church and gain 3 pool a turn. Take one down,

bin unblockably and you are back where you started.

complaining on this newsgroup. Mainly just people asking rules
questions, posting decks, tourney reports, etc. But there has been a

You can't be serious... Imbued with Travis and Church can bloat for 3
pool a turn *without playing a card*. Sure, some vampire with dominate
can bloat with Govern for 3 pool a turn, but he needs a Govern in his
hand every turn, and spends a blood every turn. Imbued can very easily
set this up to do it for free (costs them convictions, but those tend
to multiply with terrifying rapidity). Putting down Anarch Revolts are
going to probably increase the chance an Imbued deck is going to win,
especially if other narky players start blocking their prey going
anarch. The Imbued player can also block or Champion THEIR prey going
anarch. Their prey probably also isn't bloating for 3 pool a turn.
There is of course a finite limit to the amount of times someone can
Champion, but that's a complicated one we will leave for now.

> If someone's only answer to you is "pack anti-imbued tech", they
> deserve a good slapping.

If someone's only answer is "pack some intercept and combat", they
deserve a good slapping.

> If someone gives you a list of good, generically useful cards to use
> and you reject them all as "specifically anti-imbued tech" because you
> just don't want to adapt to the metagame, you deserve a good slapping.

No no no. People have been using good, generically useful cards in
their decks, and they have been getting thrashed by Imbued over and
over and over again. Imbued are cheap. They get to continuously put
awesome useful cards on their vampires every turn from their hand,
library, or ash heap, for free. They get a card that gives them all +1
intercept, for free. They are completely immune to many of the "good
generically useful" cards in the game (Disarm, Taste, Drawing out the
Beast, three super ultra good, and useful combat cards, not to mention
the fact they can block Daring the Dawn type stuff). They all treat
agg damage as normal. They get a master that gives them a pool once a
turn whenever any of them does an action. They get to come out of
torpor without an action.
If White Wolf printed the Imbued as a vampire clan (i.e. printed a
vampire that cost 4, had super useful cards put down on them from
anywhere in your deck, treats agg damage as normal, immune to all
frenzy cards, comes out of torpor automatically, blah blah blah blah),
they would be howled down as the most ridiculously overpowered clan in
the game.

Take Unmasking, for example. Decks with vampires might use a card like
KRCG (Imbued might also, but let's also leave that for the moment).
Imbued are different; they tend to use Unmasking. Let's compare them.
KRCG costs TWO pool and can tap (i.e. usable once between your untap
phases) to give one minion +1 intercept. Unmasking is free, and
permanently gives +1 intercept to ALL your minions (assuming you are
playing Imbued). Which one sounds better to you? When the only allies
were Garous, War Ghouls and Hordes, that wasn't so much of a problem,
because those allies couldn't get much other intercept. Imbued get
Second Sight, and also have access to a large number of action
cancelling or redirecting or screwing-around-with cards. Giving them
Unmasking is crazy. No vampire clan in the game has access to anything
remotely NEAR that good for intercept. The only thing close to it is
Anima Gathering, which is also possibly overpowered, but balanced by
the fact that it can not only be DI'ed, but also quite easily blocked.

The KRCG / Unmasking thing is also another excellent example of James'
point. Let's say you are playing S&B, and you want some ways of
thwarting other methuselahs getting out intercept locations. You might
put a couple of Suddens in your deck to cancel a KRCG, and maybe a
couple of Unnatural Disasters (gets rid of it if you don't have a
sudden in your hand at the right time). Those cards are also excellent
against many other cards and strategies. Suddens can cancel Blood
Dolls or whatever, Disaster can burn a Secure Haven that your
crosstable buddy needs removed to take down Arika, or whatever. What
do those cards do against The Unmasking? Nothing whatsoever, it's an
Event, not a Master. OK so you need to put anti-event cards in your
deck. They will really help you against Imbued, because Imbued usually
pack at least a couple of events (Unmasking and E.E.). But what about
against vampire decks? Does bugger all, since 95% of vampire decks
don't use events at all. See? Is your answer then to "put some anti-
event cards in your deck"? Is that "adapting to the metagame"? See
James' point?

> I am personally of the opinion that the metagame has yet to fully
> adapt to the imbued, and also that the imbued have yet to fully adapt
> to the metagame.

Pfft, the Imbued don't have to "adapt" to the metagame. They are just
doing their own thing, putting in all their standard cards that do
general Imbued stuff, and riding the metagame like a bitch all the way
to the (blood) bank. What "adapting" are you suggesting they do?
Putting 5 memories in all their decks, because it completely screws a
vampire on the table for 1 pool? And some Champion / Determine to
totally and permanently shut down any threatening actions from the
entire table? Oh wait they already do.
If your suggestion of vampires "adapting to the metagame" is putting
some intercept and combat in decks, people have been doing that too,
and in case you hadn't noticed yet, it hasn't really been working.

On Oct 3, 8:48 am, witness1 <jwnewqu...@bellsouth.net> wrote:
> Rush combat and intercept will "save" you against the imbued as well.

Well, as noted, Rush combat really won't save you against the Imbued--
they are incredibly resilient. They come out of the Hospital with
incredible ease (Jennie Orne) and without taking actions. Most of the
important offense for Rush decks don't work on the Imbued (as they
aren't vampires). Many important cards that make rush decks go don't
work on the Imbued (as they aren't vampires). It is possible that Rush
decks need to evolve to deal with the Imbued, but as the necessary
cards to evolve in that way don't exist, the ability to evolve is
highly limited (there is no Haven Uncovered that works on the Imbued;
there is no Taste that works on the Imbued; there is no Fame that
works on the Imbued; there is no Decapitate that works on the Imbued;
etc.)

I suspect that in their inception, there was fear that the Imbued
would be too vulnerable to combat. So they were given good combat
resilience. Which in the end turned out to be too resilient.

-Peter

Setites). The point was not that you should pack this tech against the

think of as a feature, but several other people seem to think of as a
bug.

Forgotten Labyrinth, and now Blithe Acceptance. The amount of stealth
an action can see is pretty high. So The Unmasking, combined with
Second Sight, and maybe a Discern gets me to three intercept. Which is
great, but getting much higher than that requires a much greater
investment than it would for vampires who wanted to do the same.

them a few permanent effects, maybe we can achieve some balance? I
guess not.

> thwarting other methuselahs getting out intercept locations. You might

you'd use to get around 3 guys with a Raven Spy each. THAT is adapting

particulars, but I agree with him that saying "pack anti-imbued tech"
isn't terribly helpful. However, it's often difficult to be helpful in
the abstract - if someone were to post a particular deck and ask how
it might be made better able to handle the imbued, without sacrificing
its ability to win otherwise, it would be a lot easier to help that
person.

I sort of had the same opinion of Determine - that it was break glass in
case of emergency only - until I saw some players using it very
effectively. At the EC day 1 event, I was playing an Ishtarri vote deck
preying on an Imbued deck. I had considered Imbued when I made my deck
and attempted to make a deck that would be effective against them. I
spent a long time tuning my hand for the perfect lunge. I had stealth,
Majesty, a KRC, a Secret Must be Kept and an Anarchist Uprising as well as
a Dreams of the Sphinx and a Barrens, so I could keep cycling throughout
my turn. My prey used Determine to cancel every good action card I
played, playing 4-5 of them in the same turn. I was left with having
to bleed for 1, which didn't do the job. Then my prey ousted his prey.
I kept trying, but my prey ended up sweeping because he'd just use his
Unity to make sure he always had plenty of Determines. Also, he'd kill a
new prey every turn or two, so the cost of Unity was pretty negligible and
he could absorb a few bleeds as well as the KRC I managed to get through.

far. Conviction costs are no big deal if you put enough Convictions in
your deck. Tapping isn't that costly if you were otherwise going to get
burned or ousted. I'm sure you know that Imbued decks often have a
minion advantage anyway.

ready to have one or two of my actions cancelled - I had more good things
to do, but when I ended up having 4-5 actions cancelled, I completely ran
out of juice.

Matt Morgan

unreasonable to use in the larger metagame. In some games, it gives

you draw, no matter what else happens.

plan on getting around that DPA loss one way or another (flush tech, a
homogeneous deck, whatever). If, for whatever reason, it's difficult
to fit that amount of flush tech, or you're just not likely enough to
either see the imbued at all, or capitalize on the advantage BtC gives
you, then don't bother.

On Oct 3, 1:21 pm, witness1 <jwnewqu...@bellsouth.net> wrote:
> That depends a lot on the rest of your deck. If you're also packing
> Dragonbound, I'd suggest 1 BtC and 2 Fortschritt Library (depending on
> how prevalent imbued are in your metagame). Then you fetch Dragonbound
> with Fortschritt if you're not seeing imbued, and Break the Code if
> you are. You may need a bit more flush tech (Dreams, Barrens) than you
> usually play to help you get rid of the excess, or you may be able to
> make do without.

And all of this is vastly deproving your ability to actually be
effective at winning games with such a deck--masters are at a premium
and deck space is at a premium. As a result, the deck's ability to win
on a reliable basis is being degraded in the name of making it work
better against the Imbued.

> Sure. But the statement "there's no Haven Uncovered that works on the
> Imbued" isn't really true. Which was all I was trying to get at.

Well, it is true. Haven Uncovered and Break the Code work very
differently. And Break the Code is completely Imbued specific. And
isn't a Master card. And isn't something you can reasonably use
multiples of in a given deck.

If Haven Uncovered (or some new version of the card) said "minion"
instead of "vampire", then there'd be a Haven Uncovered that works on
the imbued. Replacing Haven Uncovered with Break the Code is an
untennable solution. Adding Break the Code in along with Haven
Uncovered is either unreliable ('cause you have 1 or 2) or degrades
the deck considerably ('cause you have multiples and/or Forschritts).

> I'm not at all opposed to the idea. It also looks like the Design Team
> is headed in that direction.

Sure. But one doesn't exist yet--if the new set came with "We Know
Where You Live: Master. Place this card on a Minion. Other minions may
enter combat with this minion as a (D) action. This minion can take a
+1 stealth action to burn this card.", then we'd be getting somewhere.
But it didn't. And the last similar card (Frontal Assault) is
considerably disadvantagous against the Imbued in a way that it
doesn't really need to be.

> ? I seem to recall that someone with your initials once wrote that it
> was often a _good_ idea to wreck their predator.

No, no. I think you misunderstood. I am a vast advocate of wrecking
your prey, getting 1VP, and then playing backwards as neccessary. If
you go and read the write up from when I won a Qualifier with a Rush
deck, it is all about how I rarely ever backrushed. I am a vast
proponent of avoiding backrushing as much as possible--yeah, you gotta
back rush once and a while in most games, but in general, the less
backrushing you do, the more likely you are to actually win. Sometimes
you are *forced* to backrush extensively, but that is a sign that you
are losing anyway--if you are forced to backrush significantly to stay
alive, you are losing the game. Which sometimes is unfortunately the
case. But it isn't generally something you should be designing the
deck to do.

> Maybe I
> misunderstood. Or maybe the circumstances are always going to be
> radically different when it's an imbued predator.

Nope. When you have an Imbued predator and you are a Rush deck? Things
aren't actually that bad--back rush once and a while as necessary, and
just go forward. Not really much of a problem. When your *prey* is
imbued, however, and you are a Rush deck? Totally screwed. You aren't
going to oust them. You are going to be running up hill against a
river. Bad news.

-Peter

> Like I'm totally on the side of some combat cards that don't work

> it's partly people haven't adapted to how to beat them yet.

It isn't really a matter of adaptation. It is a matter that most of the
really important cards that make combat decks go (Haven Uncovered, Fame,
Tension, Dragonbound, Taste) don't work against the Imbued, and there
aren't viable alternatives. If you could adapt with viable alternatives,
there would be an argument here. But the viable alternatives simply
don't exist:

-Haven Uncovered: You could use Frontal, but that is just as likely to
kill you as not against the Imbued; Break the Code *only* works on the
Imbued, making it dead, like, 90% of the time.

-Fame/Tension/Dragonbound: Anarch Revolt is also just as likely to get
you killed as not, and is *much* less effective against the not imbued.

-Taste: One of the most important cards in the arsenal of the combat
deck for being viable. Doesn't work against the Imbued. No alternative.

Mind you, I have played Break the Code in every rush deck I have played
in competition since the Imbued hit the scene, and really, it doesn't
help that much. Yeah, it lets you attack them more often, and lets other
folks block them more often, but still, if the Imbued is your prey, you
simply aren't ousting them any time soon, if ever.

> Including
> a couple of copies of Break the Code for a pure rush deck doesn't seem
> unreasonable if you're planning on ousting via Fame and Tension you're
> a bit hosed otherwise. Threaten backwards and bleed forward pausing
> only to bin Travis as required.

You are hosed due to Fame and Tension (and Dragonbound) not working
against the Imbued, and these are the cards that were invented/reworded
pretty much specifically to make combat decks viable, in terms of
ousting folks. You sit behind the Imbued? Your most viable ousting
mechanisms are removed. So you get to bleed some, choke on combat cards,
and swim upstream to survive. If you don't press the Imbued (and by
"press", I mean "beat up a lot"), they get set up, gain steam, and oust
folks. If you do press the Imbued, you slow them down, don't oust them,
and eventually get ousted by either your first predator or your new
predator after you mangle your original predator and get him ousted.

7x Taste of Vitae

the Event module [2 cards]:
(remember: 1x Fortschritt Library)

* some Dreams of the Sphinx (I prefer 3x Wash + 3x Dreams)

Laying)

Lid)

Animalism: Carrion Crows, Taunt the Caged Beast, Song of Serenity
Auspex: Nose of the Hound, Telepathic Tracking, wake+bounce/intercept
Celerity: maneuvers/presses, additional strikes, Psyche, Fast Hands
Dominate: +Bleed, Graverobbing, Far Mastery, wake+bounce

Obtenebration: +Stealth, maneuver, Black Metamorphosis, Entombment

And sorry, Jeffrey, but I'm going to have to disagree with you here.
I've played against imbued extensively here (probably 20+ competitive
tournament worthy imbued decks with me playing rush combat). I've
adapted the shit out of my rush combat decks, and must admit, the
combat decks that do tend to work against the imbued, tend not to work
in any other decent table environment.

Yes, I agree that Carrion Crows combat does work, specifically when
tied in with weenie animalism and aid from bats. Unfortunately, weenie
animalism is not the strongest *rush* deck archetype, especially when
facing (A) Imbued with Flash Grenades, which is a popular choice, or
(B) any kind of S:CE decks, which are very popular everywhere, BTW, or
(C) a deck that can deal far range damage back, like gun decks, or
thrown sewer lid decks, etc.

Yes, you can pack canine hordes to get around (A), but then you are
devoting a large amount of deck space for a problem in a very few
decks. And as anyone who plays rush combat knows, deck space is not
something you can afford to waste.

Carrion crows in other combat decks may help you knock down the
Imbued, but if you were playing smartly as the Imbued player, you
wouldn't waste your conviction on anything but returning your imbued
from incapacitated, and blocking your predator from pillow facing your
imbued. Chances are, that if he is playing rush combat, he is probably
not going to waste deck space on stealth anyway. And if he is not
playing animalism weenies, you will have more minions out than he
will.

is actually quite a piss-poor percentage. 1 out of 3 is also about the
percentage of games I get help from others on the table to oust the
imbued player when I play a rush combat deck. All sorts of other
things can account for that table win that have little to do with the
strength of that carrion crows deck.

>From the sounds of things, what got you ousted from the game was more
table hate than a strong combat predator. If a deck archetype needs
table hate in order to take it down, that's usually a very good
indicator that the deck archetype is overpowered. It's tough for most
decks to win if they have table hate, especially if people have the
ability to do more than sneak-bleed their prey (i.e are capable of
going backwards or cross-table).

One thing I'd also like to just mention is "Anarch revolt". A lot of
imbued players advicate this as a better option for combat decks to
use instead of Dragonbound, Fame, et al., as they say it affects
vampires and imbued (in an even greater fashion). Anarch revolt is NOT
a viable alternative. Trust me, I've tried against a couple of imbued
decks and it has failed every time.

Firstly, every anarch revolt is another master phase gone, for
starters, and you need a whole whackload of them to oust in a timely
fashion.

Secondly, anarch revolt affects the whole table, including yourself.
It doesn't help if your imbued player is blocking all of your own
attempts to become anarch. Unless you are packing galarics etc - which
equates to less deck space devoted to combat. This makes your combat
module *much* weaker, and, in turn, causes you to oust much less
frequently then any other combat ousting module (backup bleed, fame et
al., etc.) Yes, you could also play stealth to push the generic action
through, and stealth is useful for some other actions, but generally,
as a combat deck, you usually need to pack as much combat as possible
into your deck if you dream of ousting more than a single player,
otherwise you simply run out of combat to play - especially when you
are facing little guys like the imbued that need loads of combat.

Thirdly, this also means the imbued can block their prey from becoming
anarchs as well (as was previously mentioned), making it even easier
for their prey to be ousted, and the imbued player becoming 6 pool
richer.

Forthly, if anyone is playing a vote deck with titled vamps, they are
rather just going to call the vote to burn anarch revolt, especially
on a table that you come across with little or no imbued (increasing
the likelihood of someone voting it off). You generally need the whole
table on your side to pull of anarch revolts, otherwise it just gets
voted away and your combat deck falls apart. Yes, and this has
happened repeatedly to me whenever I play anarch revolts, and I
imagine it would happen to most people the moment they start looking
like any sort of table threat - which combat-heavy decks are prone to
looking like (even when they're not).

Yes and no. Some tournaments I think should be like this, especially
qualifiers and championships, or any tournament that has a decently
large prize.

players together who may not normally play with each other (after all,
it's difficult to host 12+ players on a regular basis at somebodies
house, and even more difficult for everyone to travel the distance
every time), showcase some decks that you've been able to build that
are reasonably powerful, but are not necessarily uber-powered Master
of the Universe decks, as we call them round here.

Still, I advocate that both views of VTES tournament play have their
merit, and both should have their place. Some tournaments should be
downright balls to the wall competitive, some should be more like
conventions where people have a few games against decks and players
they don't see very often, and also promote the game in the meanwhile.
I know I've gone to a quite a few tournaments with a deck that I was
pretty sure wouldn't win, but was such an interesting concept that
people probably would be interested to see. A good example of this is
my current favorite Guruhi Restricted Vitae steal blood and farm deck.

right (lucky) environment.

Yes, it is a problem with Imbued. The rush deck that attempting to
oust you is merely one of many.

Here are some major differences:
1) For Outcast Mage deck you need at least a tremere to bring them out
- which immediately serves as a weak chain. This already allows that
player to play cards that would ordinarily have no effect, and still
get something out of them, such as Fame, Tension in the Ranks, Haven
Uncovered etc. which means at least the player won't have dead cards
in their hand.
2) Outcast Mage's have 0 hand damage, and their strike is easily
avoided by play IG, prevention, or dodges (covering pot, cel, and
for).
3) Any enviroment damage can quickly burn your Outcasts, instead of
sending them to incapacitated where they will pop out in 2 turns.
4) Outcast Mages can't outright kill your rush actions with
Determines, meaning they at least have to fight.
5) Outcast Mages take actions to bring out, and cost 3 pool - hardly
as cost-effective as the Imbued, especially if the main vamp get's
taken out very early.
6) Until you get Unmasking/Sport Bike out, using a Haven Uncovered is
sure to send your Tremere to a dirt nap, and then your whole deck
falls apart.

I'm sorry, but a single game against one type of rush deck is hardly
enough to convince me that MoM is good in other ally decks. Having
built plenty, I can say that CEL/POT/FOR rush decks are not the
easiest to get right as they need a whole lot to get going and work,
especially because the discipline spread is tough to get right and
vamps and usually requires some very high caps. The only feasible
version of them would be to use a multi-rush version, in which case
you'd be playing forced marches (which is also extra stealth to get
your rush actions through) and freak drives - at least 12 of them in
total, to make the deck feasible as a tournament worthy rush deck.

Still, I've built that kind of rush deck before, and it has loads of
weaknesses and is hardly representative of a good rush deck. For
example, if you were playing against my weenie POT/dom deck I listed
above, the chances is that I would tear your poor Outcast Mage deck
apart, as I'd probably have 1 more minion out than the number of
Outcast mages you have out in the early game, and I'd take out your
Tremere before you even got going. And you'd have to play loads of MoM
to keep up as well. MoM in this fashion, only really works in combat
decks that rely on very big cap vamps with no stealth or environment
damage - which is a small percentage of rush decks.

Ok. Let's say the skill levels are equal. Not that I meant beginning
player in terms of skill level in this instance, btw, but I meant it
more in the sense that they not heavily invested in the game (resource-
wise).

If skill levels are equal - I'd still think that some with infinite
access to any card they want is going to build a far nastier deck than
if s/he had access to only 2/3 starters and a handful of boosters.

Now, also include in this example that a huge group of players will
have access to the same resources as you - i.e. if everybody in your
playgroup had infinite access to any card they want, the level of the
decks will be substatially higher than a group in which each person in
that group has only 2/3 starters and a handful of boosters - mostly
because it is possible to build a substantially good deck using
minimal resources - but if there are a substantial number of people in
the same boat, than it becomes exceedingly more difficult to build one
that isn't going to be the same as someone elses. Having a group of
the same/similar style of decks in tournaments/social games on a
regular basis makes it harder for each of those decks in turn, as the
metagame shifts to prepare for that style of decks.

To give a case study of things here:
When 3rd Edition came out, every player who wanted to build a lethal
deck without a huge investment went out and got a couple of starters
of the !Malk deck, because it is very easy to build a lethal deck with
that precon (S&B is pretty easy to get right in alot of games). Now,
we had a long period of regular appearance of G4 !Malk in every
tournament and almost every social game.

In steps 2 problems:

1) People playing !Malk begin contesting like crazy, making it more
difficult for those !Malk decks to succeed because of lack of
resources for variety.

2) People not playing !Malk start wising up to the huge increase in
S&B decks, and, where they have access to cards, start putting in
defenses against that sort of thing, making it more difficult for
those !Malk decks to succeed because of lack of resources for variety.

> If you consider the hypothetical case of an experienced player with a
> small card collection and a beginning player who started out by
> spending lots of money on cards, I think the former is going to build
> a better deck.

Maybe the difference might not be so noticable for a *single* player
comparison - but in my original post I was talking about the
difference between resources of a playing *group*. Plus, as I said, I
wasn't talking about a beginning player in the sense of skill, but in
the sense of monetary investment into the game - which is not the same
thing. Someone who is just beginning to spend money in the game may
have played the games for years using someone else's cards, for
example.

> Regardless, I'm not sure why you think that NoR being a near-complete
> set is a bad thing, which is what you seem to be getting at. I think
> it's great that WW produced a very small, possibly self-contained set.

I never said it was a bad thing to release a set like this. (I can't
seem to find exactly what I said, and you haven't quoted me, so I'm
finding it very difficult to clarify).

My stance would be more in line with: It's relatively easy to build a
small range of very competitive Imbued-only deck with minimal
resources - say 2-4 booster boxes. For each person to build a deck
that can combat them reasonably without worrying about contestation,
and still be useful against vampire-based decks as well, requires a
much higher (IMO 2/3 x at least) investment.

In the USA, and especially in a Continentals Championship, this sort
of investment is probably more common than in the average tournament
in many other places in the world (at least, by looking at the posted
decks, people's comments etc.) Thus, it is possible that it is easier
and less of a problem to combat Imbued and vampire-based decks when
you do have access to more cards.

In a setting like ours, however, were the majority of decks built for
tournaments are 'cheap-man' decks - i.e. are built by players who have
a very limited amount of cards - it is far easier for the 'cheap-
man's' Imbued deck to run rampant and earn loads of VP's, and there
definitely is a disparity in the levels of decks between players, as
all the good cheap decks get taken very quickly, so players are forced
to chose between running the risk of playing the same decks as other
players OR play an inferior deck that will work in most conditions,
but will likely fail if it comes across, say, an imbued player.

Also, on a side note, all the cards that make Imbued powerful (such as
the ones Peter refered to) can be shared by all the imbued players on
the table - i.e. Jennie's text affects all imbued, not just the one's
that are controlled by the same methuselah. MoM affects all imbued
equally - meaning that vampire will not be able to damage or block all
the Imbued players. And powers, obviously, are commonly found in all
Imbued decks and aren't contested. Meaning, it is often as beneficial
to play on the same table as another Imbued as it is a hindrance - as
compared to two G4 !Malk sitting on the same table, even if their deck-
styles are different (one playing stealth-votes and one playing s&b
for example).

That being said - a small, self-contained set that allows for a
variety of decks to be built is a great thing, in my book, which is
why I'm equally pleased with LotN - especially since I find the
precons to be more usable for a group of players with little resources
than 3rd Ed was.

That's why I also wrote, just a few lines down:

- Garfield generally wanted the very best decks to combine more than one
element of the game (though he wasn't explicit about quite how)

However, Garfield did explicitly write about combat decks (*his* combat
decks, which aren't the same as our rush decks) as an explicit
archetype:

After Gamma I was pretty sure that I wanted to equalize the pursuit
of combat monster, sneak-and-bleed, or political decks. Ideally the
best decks would have elements of at least two of these pursuits.
After all, a few enhanced bleed cards in a Brujah combat deck can
really be an improvement.

So "combat monster" was a deck style he wanted to allow as a legitimate
pursuit; the ideal was making combinations the best, but it seems pretty
likely that he both planned for, and expected, players to not do that.
As discussed earlier, though, combat monster was a bit less explicitly
rush-y:

The combat monster strategy was pretty straightforward: if your
vampires were so deadly in combat that no one dared to block them,
you could waltz over to your prey and bleed him at will. Your
predator, on the other hand, would think twice about sending a
vampire to bleed you when she might have to face one of your servants
in combat.

So there's a likelihood of some sort of bleed for 1-get blocked, and
block people doing the same. Presumably, a few rush cards would be for
taking out people who were annoying in some specific way, or to combat a
sneak-bleed predator. Garfield talks about sneak-bleeders being able to
evade blocks and so not needing combat defence for that, so I guess rush
cards might well have been see as one reasonable way to handle that -
part of the balancing of Gamma, perhaps.

Combat resilience factors:
1) Jennie Orne text works even if she is incapacitated. A combat deck
needs to burn her outright to stop the imbued from popping out of
hospital all of the time.
2) Imbued don't worry about agg, making all agg-damage related combat
decks almost entirely useless.
3) You can't taste Imbued - ensuring that they will probably wear your
combat deck down slowly, especially if they start using their strikes
with conviction. This is bigger than most people realise - combat
decks need to keep gaining their blood back to keep going, otherwise
they end up in torpor more often than their opponents - combat is
costly (as a general rule).
4) You can't Fame/Dragonbound/Path of Lilith them, and Tension in the
Ranks and Frontal Assualt only works when you burn them. This makes
sure it's really difficult for a rush combat deck to oust them without
strapping on another ousting method (like bleed or vote).
5) You can't play Haven Uncovered on them, and many of your rush cards
can simply be determined away.
6) Imbued use conviction use all their powers - not blood/life, so
being on one life after they bounce out of hospital is fine for them,
so long as they can keep avoiding combat or bouncing out of hospital.

Fixing Memories of Mortality for the Imbued will help combat decks
defeat them, but the Imbued would still be pretty damn resilient
against combat decks. They may not win with a combat deck on it's
tail, but the chances of the combat deck winning are pretty slim
(unless, as has been said, you strap on another ousting strategy to
them, like vote or bleed).

No, without MoM she is incapacitated. Her text still works while she
is incapacitated. Getting her dead i.e. burnt, is a little more
tricky. She needs to be burnt for her text not to affect the game.

>
> > 2) Imbued don't worry about agg, making all agg-damage related combat
> > decks almost entirely useless.
>
> Irrelevant, because agg combat sucks balls anyway. And there are

Agg combat was at least a viable way to win a tourney. Now it isn't.
That is a BIG difference in my books. Vampire's may have plenty of
ways to prevent agg damage - but I'd hardly say they were in the
majority of tournament decks (with 2 agg being the average they'd need
to prevent on a regular basis), and especially not in big numbers. At
least, that has been my experience here. S:CE is a far greater and
more prevalent tool for combat defence.

> > 3) You can't taste Imbued - ensuring that they will probably wear your
> > combat deck down slowly, especially if they start using their strikes
> > with conviction. This is bigger than most people realise - combat
> > decks need to keep gaining their blood back to keep going, otherwise

> is still in hospital though.

Yes, but with the Vampire not filling up, he becomes a weaker
opponent, and soon he is unable to play his cards or take the little
bit of damage you are dealing him, and then it's dirt nap time. And
once your vamp takes a dirt nap, good luck getting him out, cos you'll
need stealth and blood everytime. Hence the Imbued will out-survive
the combat deck, making them combat resilient.

> > 4) You can't Fame/Dragonbound/Path of Lilith them, and Tension in the
> > Ranks and Frontal Assualt only works when you burn them. This makes
> > sure it's really difficult for a rush combat deck to oust them without
> > strapping on another ousting method (like bleed or vote).

> Irrelevant. We aren't talking about pool damage here at the moment,
> but whether Imbued are resilient to combat. And anyway, combat decks
> shouldn't rely solely on ousting with Fame/Dragonbound/Path/Tension
> but should also be capable of old fashion ousting (bleed). Weenie
> combat decks, (the most viable before Imbued) are perfect for doing
> this, because Imbued only have so many wakes. Bleed en masse is fine.

First - as I said - without strapping on another ousting method.
Bleed, vote and combat should each be able to oust in their own right,
even though I believe having multiple methods of ousting is generally
better. The big problem there is that combat decks are notoriously
difficult to find space with. Other ousting methods take up space.

That being said - combat decks shouldn't be forced to become bruise-
bleed decks. They should have a reasonable chance of ousting their
prey, just like the other deck types do.

The issue you brought up was that Imbued are combat resilient. Telling
me that combat decks should rely on other ousting methods as well, is
already admitting that the Imbued are resilient to combat decks
ousting methods.

> As to Imbued not being affected by these cards, it's moot - they still
> end up in hospital or burned.
>

The thing is that the Imbued Meth will usually survive - hence they
are resilient to combat decks.

>

> get into combat, if you cannot succeed in rush, bleed with all of your
> minions and watch them start to block you. Eventually you'll get
> them. And anyway, I've had pretty decent success bleeding forward and
> rushing back with my combat decks. Eventually, they will be forced to

Again, this means your deck becomes a bleed deck, or a vote deck, with
combat as a way of delivering the payload.

> > 6) Imbued use conviction use all their powers - not blood/life, so
> > being on one life after they bounce out of hospital is fine for them,
> > so long as they can keep avoiding combat or bouncing out of hospital.
>
> Irrelevant. When they bounce out of hospital they have 1 life, it's
> pretty easy to do 1 more point of damage to them. If they bounce out
> of hospital, they generally have 0 convictions. If they are doing the
> hospital yo-yo dance, then they aren't really being resilient are
> they?

Yes, but when they do the yo-yo dance, you were lucky enough to (A)
get into combat with them, and (B) play enough cards that they
couldn't get out of the combat. Having to do this repeatedly quickly
depletes your resources, but does nothing to them, as their conviction
keeps coming back.

> > Fixing Memories of Mortality for the Imbued will help combat decks
> > defeat them, but the Imbued would still be pretty damn resilient
> > against combat decks. They may not win with a combat deck on it's
> > tail, but the chances of the combat deck winning are pretty slim
> > (unless, as has been said, you strap on another ousting strategy to
> > them, like vote or bleed).
>
> Every deck has bleed as a strategy (unless you're playing a Martin
> Frankle Superstar deck).

I beg to differ. Every deck is able to bleed. Not every deck has a
bleed strategy. Just like every deck is able to vote (given that they
are able to get the edge), not every deck has a vote strategy. A
strategy would have to include cards that improve the damage you do
while bleeding, otherwise it's not a strategy.

> Weenie decks excel at bleeding, with or
> without cards. 5 minions bleeding for 1 every turn is more than most
> decks can handle for long, especially if it is backed up with brutal
> combat.

Weenies are just one form of combat decks. And weenies can be knocked
down fairly easily by the Imbued, and will have a much harder time
recovering than the Imbued will.

>
> You have not really argued successfully that Imbued are combat
> resilient, indeed you have missed that angle pretty much entirely.
>

I have argued very successfully, it's that you are arguing a different
and much smaller point, and from a different viewpoint than the issues
that people have brought up here. You are coming from the viewpoint
that you think it will be difficult for the Imbued to win with a
strong combat deck predator, especially if MoM is no longer in the
picture. I agree with you there, on the most part. However, the
general point has always been, and still remains, that combat decks
struggle to oust the Imbued, and that's the straw that broke the
camel's back, as far as playing combat decks in tournaments go.

The argument about combat decks are that they have difficulty ousting
an imbued prey.

Your argument is that, without MoM, it's much easier for combat decks
to dunk the Imbued.
At least, that's as much as you have proved.

My argument is, "So what? Just cos we can dunk the Imbued, doesn't
mean we can oust them."

Weenie combat decks have their minions dunked just as much as the
Imbued do, but have a much harder time getting out of torpor, plus
they have a difficult time entering combat - no Haven's, frontals
really bad for them, no other funky permanent rushes, like blood
hunts.

Multi-rush combat decks (i.e. freak-drivers), which are the worst
affected by MoM, still struggle cos they need to find ways of getting
blood back fast enough without tastes.

A standard combat deck that doesn't fall under one of these two
categories, relies on a 3 vamp average. Either they are forced to go
full-tilt at their Imbued prey, in which case they are leaving
themselves wide open for their predator, or the Imbued get to do the
yo-yo dance, cos they'll block your pillow-facing, and you have
roughly 2 actions a turn to do something to your prey (dunk and
blocked pillow-face attempt). For most imbued, this level of recovery
is a joke if you have Jennie alive, and still pretty feasible if you
don't. You would have to dunk the blocker in each and every single
combat to make this even remotely feasible - which would mean a really
good hand for you, and/or little/no combat defence in theirs (i.e. no
flash grenades, manuevers with guns, surge etc.) Plus, you'd need to
get sufficient rush right - which is again, highly unlikely, cos
bleeding with two minions for 1 bleed is laughable. The Imbued can
easily handle that.

Your solution to my issue is, well, strap on some bleed. My response
is that combat decks should not be forced to become bleeding decks in
order to be playable in a tournament. They were feasible before and
they should remain so. Even before Imbued, getting a combat deck right
was tricky. Now it's nearly impossible.

capabilities.
